correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the two product-idempotence conditions to alpha beta alpha = alpha and beta alpha beta = beta for the image-restricted maps, valid in both directions. It counts image choices, selected fiber representatives, free assignments and their complement bijectively. All summation ranges and factors are defined for every n>=1. An independent brute-force full-function census confirms every coefficient for n=1..6, but only the combinatorial bijection proves the universal result.

originality.rationale: The complete reviewed 2021 article proves type-existence thresholds for partial transformations, while the available 2006 full-transformation abstract advertises four types and their ubiquity. The proposed theorem instead gives every labeled pair-rank coefficient as an explicit all-n sum; neither inspected stated result implies those numerical multiplicities. Closest mathematically related enumerative work is on different semigroups or different parameters. No absolute priority certification is asserted; 2006 full-text access and uncatalogued equivalent formulas remain risks.

value.rationale: The central question of which idempotent transformations form skew pairs is a motivated semigroup-structure problem with an established taxonomy. A full joint-rank distribution across all n is a natural and previously unstated enumerative invariant: it resolves the sizes of every labeled rank stratum, detects the minimal full-monoid threshold, and yields a closed rank-(2,2) formula. This is not merely a numerical table or a routine reformulation of the 2006/2021 existence theorems. Further structural orbit/subtype investigations could use these coefficients as benchmark data.
